title: Auth
purpose: Sign in, sign up, verify, pass two-factor and reset a password without revealing whether an account exists.
useWhen: A product authenticates people with passwords, SSO, emailed links or one-time codes.
avoidWhen: Re-confirming identity before one sensitive action inside the product; use the consequential-action contract with the provider's re-authentication.
alternatives: Use the provider's hosted sign-in page when the product delegates authentication entirely.
requiredInputs: step adapters that never reveal whether an account exists
transitions: sign-in → submitting → two-factor or signed-in, or credentials-rejected keeping the email
credentials-rejected → rate-limited after the service's limit
sign-in → link-sent, with a resend after a countdown
applicability: Sign-in, sign-up, verification, two-factor and password reset screens.
exceptions: Require only the methods the product offers; the security of authentication itself is the application's.
